source_read: PDF of the scanned print pages, Chest 107(5), pp. 1237-1241 (5 page images). The OCR text layer was used only to find passages; every number below was read on 150-dpi renderings, and Tables 1 and 2 on 300-dpi crops. p. 1241 holds the last references and an advertisement; no supplement.

claims.overstatement: None for the part from this source; the claim frames the 0 of 25 with its interval and does not repeat the authors' 'appears to be safe'. One linkage to watch: 'In that 29-hospital series' follows the sentence giving, second-hand, complications in 38% of 130 patients, 90% within 12 hours and no in-hospital deaths. This paper reports in-hospital outcomes only for the 66 ECG-eligible patients (Table 2) and contains no 38% or 90% figure and no outcome for the other 64 of the 130; those figures must come from another report of the same series (the editors should check which paper McCord et al. cite for them). The claim's own wording for this paper ('no one died in hospital among the 66') is correct.
claims.note: Checked on the scan: 29 acute-care institutions (abstract, p. 1237; 29 centres listed in the Acknowledgment, p. 1240); 1987 to 1993; 136 infarctions in 130 patients; 25 thrombolysed and 41 ECG-eligible but not thrombolysed (66 in all); no in-hospital deaths in either group; no intracerebral haemorrhage or bleeding needing transfusion attributed to thrombolysis (0%, printed 95% CI 0 to 12%); 2 minor complications (febrile reaction after streptokinase; vaginal bleeding without transfusion); 1 fatal intracerebral haemorrhage among 11 earlier case reports, 1 in 36 (2.8%) overall. Editors' calculation recomputed: exact two-sided 95% CI for 0/25 = 0 to 13.72% (claim 13.7%, same); the printed 12% equals 3/25, the rule-of-three approximation. 'By their clinicians' decision' is a fair reading (retrospective chart review; abstract: 'Interventions: None'; co-treatment not standardized, p. 1239). 'Patients who were given the treatment but turned out not to have an infarction were not included' is correct: entry required infarction by international criteria plus the attending physician's impression (p. 1237), and the authors note that in one series 43% of chest-pain patients met TIMI criteria without infarction (p. 1239). Not used by the claim but relevant to it: the authors cite a major-complication-or-death risk under 2% for thrombolysis in patients without cocaine use (p. 1239), so 0 of 25 cannot show a similar risk; 1 of 36 has an exact 95% CI of 0.07 to 14.5% (editors' calculation). Case-finding also reviewed every infarction chart of patients aged 40 or under for cocaine use (p. 1237), which skews the series young and fits the claim's 'mostly young men' (mean age about 38-40; men 73% and 88% in the two groups).

anchors.extracted: Retrospective cross-sectional survey at 29 acute-care institutions; patients with cocaine-associated myocardial infarction 1987-1993 found by medical record review; 25 given thrombolytic therapy compared with 41 whose ECG met TIMI criteria but who were not given it. No major complications or deaths among the 25 (95% CI printed 0 to 12%); minor complications in 2. Authors conclude thrombolysis appears safe but its value is unclear and further study is needed before routine use.

Cases found by crossing ICD-9 codes for myocardial infarction with codes for cocaine and/or drug abuse, plus review of the records of all infarction patients aged 40 or under for evidence of cocaine use. All three required: cocaine use in the 24 hours before presentation by history or cocaine metabolites in urine; infarction by international diagnostic criteria and the attending physician's clinical impression; initial ECG meeting TIMI criteria for thrombolysis. Thrombolysed patients compared with ECG-eligible patients who were not thrombolysed.

Serial cardiac isoenzymes every 8 to 12 hours; complications recorded (heart failure, ventricular and supraventricular arrhythmias, bradydysrhythmias, ventricular rupture, septal perforation, death). For thrombolysed patients the agent, regimen, clinical reperfusion and complications attributable to thrombolysis were abstracted; intracerebral haemorrhage and bleeding needing transfusion counted as major complications.

136 cocaine-associated myocardial infarctions in 130 patients. After excluding those not meeting TIMI criteria, 25 had received thrombolytic therapy and 41 met the ECG criteria but had not; the groups did not differ in demographics, history, time from last cocaine use, chest-pain duration, ECG distribution of infarction or nitroglycerin use (Table 1).

No deaths during hospitalization in either group (25 and 41). No major complication (intracerebral haemorrhage or need for transfusion) attributed to thrombolysis: 0%, 95% CI printed 0 to 12%. Two minor complications: a self-limited, untreated febrile reaction after streptokinase, and vaginal bleeding attributed to thrombolysis that did not need transfusion. Editors' calculation: exact 95% CI for 0/25 is 0 to 13.7%; 0 deaths in 66 has an exact upper limit of 5.4%.

Not thrombolysed (n=41) vs thrombolysed (n=25): mean age 38.1 (SD 9.8) vs 39.8 (SD 10.3); men 73% vs 88%; nonwhite 83% vs 64%; last cocaine use under 4 hours 39% vs 40%, under 24 hours 81% vs 64%; Q-wave 46% vs 56%; nitroglycerin 85% vs 96%; aspirin 49% vs 76%; calcium-channel blockers 17% vs 24%; beta-adrenergic blockade 5% vs 32% (no p-values for the last three). Editors' Fisher tests on reconstructed counts: aspirin p=0.04, beta-blockade p=0.005.

In-hospital complications after arrival, not thrombolysed vs thrombolysed: heart failure 7% vs 4%; sustained ventricular tachycardia 2% vs 0%; supraventricular tachycardia 2% vs 8%; bradydysrhythmias 10% vs 12%; death during acute care 0% vs 0%; all NS. Median peak CK 1,115 (562-2,669) vs 1,911 (763-3,580) U/L.

Thrombolysis carries a risk of major complications or death under 2% in patients with infarction not related to cocaine (cited trial); of 11 previously reported patients given thrombolysis for cocaine-associated infarction, 1 had an intracerebral haemorrhage that resulted in death.

25 treated in this series without major complications and with 2 minor ones; with the earlier case reports, 1 intracerebral haemorrhage among 36 thrombolysed patients (2.8%). Editors' calculation: exact 95% CI for 1/36 is 0.07% to 14.5%.
The sample is too small to compare thrombolysis complication rates between patients who do and do not use cocaine; the authors say only that the risk does not appear high enough to prohibit use.

ECGs reported abnormal in 56% to 84% of patients with cocaine-associated chest pain; in one series 43% met TIMI criteria though none had an infarction; how many patients are thrombolysed on ECG criteria without infarction is unknown (such patients are outside this study's entry criteria).

Survival is unlikely to be a useful end point because mortality from cocaine-associated infarction is low, 0% in this series; prospective studies of ventricular function and artery patency with standardized co-treatment are needed before widespread use.
29 participating centres listed by US region: 16 Northeast, 2 Southeast, 2 Southwest, 3 Northwest, 6 Midwest; mostly urban teaching and municipal hospitals.

key_findings.correction: The 14 of 21 (67%) is in the Results (p. 1238); the 'two or more signs' rule appears only in the Discussion, 4th paragraph (p. 1239), as the card's locator says.
The Results text calls the times to peak 'mean' (p. 1238); Table 2 does not say whether they are means or medians.

Recomputed for race: chi-square 0.082, Yates 0.149, Fisher 0.137; 33/41 = 80.5% rounds to 80%, so 81% is not attainable with 41 (a different denominator through missing timing data is possible but not stated).
Page p. 1240 with the locator's note that the 8th paragraph begins on p. 1239 is accurate; the recommendation of a cautious policy is the 9th paragraph, p. 1240.

reporting_issues.note: The abbreviation box on p. 1237 reads CK-MB = creatine kinase.
Recomputed: race chi-square 0.082 / Yates 0.149 / Fisher 0.137; sex 0.153 / 0.263 / 0.218; use within 24 h 0.137 / 0.232 / 0.157. All fall in the card's ranges.
If 25 and 41 count patients, 64 of the 130 were excluded (editors' arithmetic), but the paper does not say so.

risk_of_bias.note: ROBINS-I fits a non-randomized comparison of a hospital treatment; overall 'serious' follows the worst domains. As the card says, for the claim's use (counts in the treated group and in-hospital deaths among the 66) the binding problems are selection (confirmed infarction required) and imprecision rather than confounding.

interpretation_gap.note: 'Substantial' is right: the headline 'appears to be safe' rests on 0 of 25, compatible with up to 13.7% against the under-2% the authors cite for patients without cocaine use.

missed: Outcomes are reported only for the 66 ECG-eligible patients; the paper gives no in-hospital course for the other patients of the 130 and contains no overall complication rate (for example 38%) or timing of complications (for example 90% within 12 hours). The card might say so, because cl_coc_chest_pain_mi links second-hand figures for all 130 patients to 'that 29-hospital series'; the 'mortality ... 0% in this series' phrase (p. 1240) does not say which denominator it means.
Minor: the Acknowledgment places Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Memphis (p. 1240); no effect on any finding.
